summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Lahdo Traitor 2/18)

data.turoyo: <...> Hawxa mazʕaqle bəṯri omər yaʕni: "Papaz papaz!" Yaʕni qašo qašo, hawxa mqašmalle aʕli.
data.translation: <...> He shouted at med: papazpapaz, which means “vicar vicar”. Thus he made fun of me, so to say.

rationale: New Preterit box; overt mocking act and ʕal-marked target.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC NE Samson the hero/22)

data.turoyo: <...> Hooo, komqašməri aʕle, ʕayne kanné biṭe, iḏoṯe kanné mәṣre, ŭ zənǧər harke ŭ harke, ha hawxa kanné iḏe mәṣre bu+zənǧər.
data.translation: <...> Oooh, they mock at him, his eyes, there they are, burst, his hands, there they are bound, and a chain, here and here, just like so, there are his hands, tied with the chain.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; explicit scene establishes mockery with ʕal target.

data.turoyo: Warḥasəl Ṭayre Simər aṯi, mbele i ḥreto ste. Fayiši dlo bəndar, veǧa ann aḥunone komoḥile w komaqašmri ebe.
data.translation: Um es kurz zu machen: Der Vogel Simurgh holte die letzte Schwester. Nun blieben sie ohne Hausfrau. Da schlugen sie ihn und verspotteten ihn.

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; b-marked target contrasts with the inherited aʕle.

data.turoyo: Kogəḥki aʕle, komqašmri ebe: "Aydarbo elux mṭelux a tlaṯ?"
data.translation: Sie lachen über ihn, machen sich lustig über ihn: "Wieso hast du die drei geholt?"

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; overt mocking speech and coordination with laughing.

data.turoyo: <...> Hanək an naʕime ne, kəmqašmri ʕal ar rabe bu waxt.
data.translation: <...> Das sind die Kinder, die sich zu ihrer Zeit über die großen lustig machen. -

rationale: Fifth Infectum example; lexical ʕal-marked target rather than a pronoun.

summary: All seven records fit I.1 mockery. Keep the glossary's I classification for this four-consonant root; Q in the reader's morphological shorthand does not establish a new glossary stem.
Lahdo Traitor 2/18 supplies the missing Preterit box, with mqašmalle plausibly showing r+l assimilation. Calling the priest papaz is the mocking act, not a lexical idiom of qšmr.

Infectum targets are expressed with ʕal/aʕl- (Samson, children mocking adults) and b-/ebe (67/56; 67/103). Both are already licensed by the inherited gloss, so no government change or new sense is needed.

The prefixed and bare Infectum in the Samson episode describe the same activity; one context is selected. Coordination with laughing is compositional, with no evidence for a separate light-verb collocation.
The source etymology remains unknown. These occurrences alone do not determine the contact source.
Confirm the derivation/etymology of qšmr; the corpus supports the paradigm and meaning but cannot identify a donor.
Confirm r+l assimilation in mqašmalle against the preferred paradigm.
